cards.benefit_text: The scheme provides cashless hospitalization coverage up to ₹5,00,000 per family per year. It includes consultation, medicines, diagnostics, surgery, ICU, implants, accommodation and food, plus 3 days pre‑hospitalisation and 15 days post‑hospitalisation expenses, and covers pre‑existing diseases.
cards.who_can_apply: Rural families that meet any deprivation criterion such as a single kucha house, no adult aged 16‑59, disabled with no able‑bodied adult, SC/ST, landless manual labourers or destitute households are covered. Urban workers such as ragpickers, domestic workers, street vendors, construction labourers and sweepers are also covered.
cards.documents: Required documents include age and identity proof such as Aadhaar or PAN card, proof of address, and an income certificate. The CSC centre will tell you the full list of papers.
cards.how_to_apply: Visit a hospital or Community Service Centre. An Arogya Mitra searches the beneficiary list using name, location, ration card or mobile number. Provide Aadhaar and ration card for identification and upload scanned documents to receive the e‑card.

cards.benefit_text: The scheme gives a guaranteed minimum pension of Rs. 1000, Rs. 2000, Rs. 3000, Rs. 4000 or Rs. 5000 per month after age 60 until death. The spouse receives the same pension after the subscriber’s death. The nominee gets the accumulated pension wealth after both die.
cards.who_can_apply: People aged 18 to 40 can join. There is no income requirement. Citizens who are or have been income tax payers are not eligible.
cards.documents: Active bank or post office savings account for KYC, Aadhaar for identity verification, and Aadhaar virtual ID or XML file for KYC upload. The CSC centre will tell you the full list of papers.
cards.how_to_apply: Visit the eNPS website and select Atal Pension Yojana. Fill basic and nominee details, choose the pension amount and contribution frequency, give consent for auto‑debit, and complete Aadhaar KYC by OTP or uploading the XML/Virtual ID.

cards.benefit_text: The scheme brings one member, preferably a woman, from each rural poor household into a Self Help Group network. Women SHGs get bank linkage, capacity building, livelihood promotion and financial inclusion. Revolving funds and interest subvention support SHG credit.
cards.who_can_apply: Self Help Groups that have been active for at least six months and follow regular meetings, savings, inter‑loaning, timely repayment and up‑to‑date accounts are eligible. Groups graded by NABARD standards qualify. Defunct groups can join after reviving for three months.
cards.documents: Aadhar number, proof of identity, proof of residence, voter ID card, passport size photo are required. The CSC centre will tell you the full list of papers.
cards.how_to_apply: Visit the DAY‑NRLM registration portal online. Fill mandatory fields such as name, email and contact number. Provide a username, create and confirm a password, then click Create New Account.

cards.benefit_text: The scheme pays Rs.300/- per month to disabled people between 18 and 79 years. The scheme pays Rs.500/- per month to disabled people aged 80 years and above.
cards.who_can_apply: People aged 18 years and above can apply. Applicants are residents of India with disability more than 80%. Applicants belong to Below Poverty Line and dwarfs are also included.
cards.documents: Papers needed are BPL Card and Aadhaar card and disability certificate. Age proof and passport size photographs are also needed. The CSC centre will tell you the full list of papers.
cards.how_to_apply: People apply online through UMANG App and search for NSAP. People fill basic details and choose mode of payment of pension. People upload photo and submit the form.

cards.benefit_text: The scheme pays 300 rupees per month to widows between 40 years and 79 years. The scheme pays 500 rupees per month to persons who are 80 years and above.
cards.who_can_apply: Widows in the age group of 40 to 79 years can apply. Widows must belong to a household living below the poverty line.
cards.documents: The papers are death certificate of husband with name of widow. BPL card is needed. Age proof like birth certificate or school certificate is needed. The CSC centre will tell you the full list of papers.
cards.how_to_apply: People use UMANG App and search for NSAP. People login with mobile number and OTP. People fill basic details and upload photo and submit.

cards.benefit_text: The scheme pays cash for delivery in a health institution. In Low Performing States the payment is ₹1,400/- for rural areas and ₹1,000/- for urban areas. In High Performing States the payment is ₹700/- for rural areas and ₹600/- for urban areas.
cards.who_can_apply: Pregnant women delivering in a government health centre or accredited private institution can apply. In High Performing States applicants are from Below Poverty Line households or are Scheduled Caste or Scheduled Tribe women. Home delivery support is for Below Poverty Line households.
cards.documents: Important papers are Below Poverty Line certificate, Scheduled Caste certificate, Scheduled Tribe certificate and Maternal And Child Health Card. The Janani Suraksha Yojana Card and referral slip are also needed at the time of delivery. The CSC centre will tell you the full list of papers.
cards.how_to_apply: Registration is done through Accredited Social Health Activist, Auxiliary Nurse Midwife or Anganwadi Worker at government health centres. The worker fills the Maternal and Child Health Card. People carry Below Poverty Line certificate and referral slip for delivery.

cards.benefit_text: Banks give crop loans through the Kisan Credit Card. The first year limit covers crop cost and area plus 10% for home needs and 20% for farm repairs. Later years add 10% for higher costs. Term loans cover land and farm tools.
cards.who_can_apply: Farmers who own land and farm alone or together can apply. Tenant farmers and share croppers can also apply. Groups of farmers who work together can also apply.
cards.documents: Two photos and the filled form are needed. ID proof like Aadhar Card is needed. Address proof and land papers from revenue office are needed. The CSC centre will tell you the full list of papers.
cards.how_to_apply: People can go to the bank website and choose Kisan Credit Card. People fill the form and press submit. The bank gives a reference number and contacts in 3-4 working days.

cards.benefit_text: The scheme gives guaranteed employment within 15 days from date of application. Work is within 5 kilometers of residence if possible and inside the Block. Wages are paid within a week or fifteen days at most.
cards.who_can_apply: Applicants must be at least 18 years of age. Applicants must live in a rural area.
cards.documents: Applicants need a photograph. Proof of identity like ration card, voter ID card, Aadhaar or PAN is needed. Name, age and gender details of household members are needed. The CSC centre will tell you the full list of papers.
cards.how_to_apply: Applicants go to the local Gram Panchayat office. Applicants give an application on plain paper or make an oral request before the Panchayat Secretary. Applicants give names of adult household members willing to do unskilled manual work.

cards.benefit_text: The scheme gives training in Designated Trades and Optional Trades. Government pays 25% of stipend up to Rs.1,500 per month through bank transfer. Minimum stipend is Rs.5,000 to Rs.9,000 per month based on schooling and certificates.
cards.who_can_apply: Apprentices must be 14 to 35 years old. Age is 18 years for hazardous trades. Candidates need Aadhaar number and e-KYC on the apprenticeship portal.
cards.documents: Aadhaar Card is needed for registration. Documents required as per selected trade are needed. The CSC centre will tell you the full list of papers.
cards.how_to_apply: Candidates go to the official Apprenticeship Portal and choose register as candidate. Candidates enter mobile number and email ID with Aadhaar number. Candidates complete e-KYC and mobile OTP authentication.

cards.benefit_text: The scheme pays 20000 rupees as lump sum assistance on death of the breadwinner. The money is for the surviving head of the household found after local inquiry.
cards.who_can_apply: The applicant must be a citizen of India. The family must live Below Poverty Line. The deceased breadwinner was more than 18 years and less than 60 years and the applicant is the succeeding primary breadwinner.
cards.documents: The important papers are death certificate and BPL card. Proof of identity and bank account details are also needed. The CSC centre will tell you the full list of papers.
cards.how_to_apply: The form is available free at the District Social Welfare Officer or Tehsil Social Welfare Officer. The filled form with documents is submitted to the designated officer.

cards.benefit_text: The scheme pays ₹3,000/- every month after sixty years of age. The Government of India puts matching money every month. After death, the spouse is entitled to fifty per cent as family pension.
cards.who_can_apply: Shop owners, retail traders, and self-employed people can apply. Applicants must be between 18 and 40 years of age. Annual turnover must not be more than ₹1,50,00,000/-.
cards.documents: Applicants need Aadhaar Card. Bank account details and Indian Financial System Code are needed. Bank passbook or bank statement is needed as proof. The CSC centre will tell you the full list of papers.
cards.how_to_apply: Applicants must visit the nearest Common Service Centre for registration. Aadhaar Card and bank account proof must be taken. The Village Level Entrepreneur fills details and collects first payment in cash.

cards.benefit_text: The scheme pays a monthly pension. It pays 200 rupees up to 79 years. It pays 500 rupees after that.
cards.who_can_apply: Applicants must be citizens of India. They must live Below Poverty Line. They must be at least 60 years of age.
cards.documents: Important papers are Aadhar Number and Bank Passbook. Ration Card and age proof are also needed. A filled application form is needed. The CSC centre will tell you the full list of papers.
cards.how_to_apply: Applications are online through UMANG App. Citizens login with mobile number and OTP. Citizens search for NSAP and fill basic details with photo.

cards.benefit_text: The scheme pays Rs. 6000 per annum per family. The money is paid in three equal installments of Rs 2000 each. Each installment comes every four months.
cards.who_can_apply: Landholding farmer families can apply. The family must have cultivable land in its name.
cards.documents: The papers needed are Aadhaar Card and landholding papers. A savings bank account is also needed. The CSC centre will tell you the full list of papers.
cards.how_to_apply: The application is done via CSCs. The VLE fills the farmer registration details. Farmers carry Aadhaar Card and landholding papers and savings bank account.

cards.benefit_text: The scheme gives a registration certificate with 100 rupees on the NFDP platform. The scheme pays success fees of 3000 to 5000 rupees after bank loan disbursement. The scheme gives a one time insurance incentive and a performance grant.
cards.who_can_apply: People and groups working in fisheries value chain can apply for registration on NFDP. Fish farmers with aquaculture farms up to 4hectares can apply for the insurance incentive. Micro and small enterprises working in fisheries can apply for the performance grant.
cards.documents: People need Aadhar number linked with mobile and bank account details. People need loan disbursement certificate or loan account statement from the bank. People need aquaculture insurance policy papers and farm size details. The CSC centre will tell you the full list of papers.
cards.how_to_apply: People can apply online or through CSCs. People start new user registration on the NFDP home page. People need Aadhar number or PAN card number with linked mobile for OTP validation.

cards.benefit_text: The scheme gives loans up to ₹10,000 to street vendors to restart and expand business. The interest rate is 7%. No collateral is needed. No processing fee is charged. The repayment period is one year.
cards.who_can_apply: Street vendors with Certificate of Vending or Identity Card from Urban Local Bodies can apply. Vendors identified in the survey but without the certificate or card can also apply. Vendors with a Letter of Recommendation from Urban Local Bodies or Town Vending Committee can apply.
cards.documents: Important papers are Certificate of Vending, Identity Card and Letter of Recommendation. Aadhaar Card and PAN Card are also needed as identity proof. The CSC centre will tell you the full list of papers.
cards.how_to_apply: Applications can be made online and offline. The form is filled online with vendor category and Survey Reference Number. Relevant documents are uploaded and the form is submitted.

cards.benefit_text: The scheme pays 1,20,000 rupees per house in plain areas. It pays 1,30,000 rupees per house in hilly areas and difficult areas. It also pays up to 12,000 rupees for toilets. Houses are at least 25 sq m with space for clean cooking.
cards.who_can_apply: Houseless households and households in zero, one or two room houses with kutcha walls and kutcha roofs can apply. Priority is for households without shelter, destitute households, manual scavengers, primitive tribal groups and released bonded laborers. Gram Sabhas verify the list from SECC 2011.
cards.documents: People need Aadhaar number and Aadhaar card copy. People need MGNREGA job card and bank account details. People also need an affidavit saying the family owns no pucca house. The CSC centre will tell you the full list of papers.
cards.how_to_apply: People can register on the official PMAY-G website. People fill personal details, bank details, MGNREGA job card number and SBM number. The concerned office fills the last section.

cards.benefit_text: The scheme helps set up new micro enterprises. Banks give a loan and the scheme pays subsidy. Maximum project cost is ₹50,00,000 for manufacturing and ₹20,00,000 for service. Special group pays 05% and the scheme pays 35% in rural areas.
cards.who_can_apply: People above 18 years of age can apply. There is no income limit. Only new projects are allowed and one person from one family can apply.
cards.documents: The application needs caste certificate and rural area certificate and project report and education certificate. The CSC centre will tell you the full list of papers.
cards.how_to_apply: People go to the official PMEGP portal and choose application for new unit. People fill the form and upload the papers and submit.

cards.benefit_text: Premiums are up to 2 % for Kharif crops, 1.5 % for Rabi crops and 5 % for horticultural crops. Government subsidizes the rest and pays premiums in North‑Eastern States, Jammu, Kashmir and Himachal Pradesh. Scheme covers natural disasters, pests, diseases and post‑harvest losses, and settles claims quickly.
cards.who_can_apply: All farmers, tenant farmers and sharecroppers who grow notified crops in notified areas can apply. Applicants must have an insurable interest in the crops and a valid land ownership certificate or tenancy agreement. Applications must be made within two weeks of sowing season start.
cards.documents: Passport‑sized photograph, identity proof such as Aadhaar or PAN, land record documents like RoR or LPC, and a declaration about the crop sown. The CSC centre will tell you the full list of papers.
cards.how_to_apply: Visit the PMFBY official website, click Farmer Corner and select Guest Farmer to register. After registration, log in, fill the application form, upload required documents and choose to pay later or make payment.

cards.benefit_text: The scheme gives one-year term life cover of ₹ 2.00 Lakh. It covers death due to any reason. The premium is ₹ 436/- per annum per subscriber. The premium is auto debited from bank or post office account.
cards.who_can_apply: People aged 18 to 50 Years can apply. Applicants must hold an individual bank or post office account.
cards.documents: The form asks for self-attested copies of required papers. The CSC centre will tell you the full list of papers.
cards.how_to_apply: Applicants fill and sign the consent-cum-declaration form. Applicants attach self-attested copies of required papers. Applicants submit the case to the official of the bank or post office.

cards.benefit_text: The scheme pays a minimum assured pension of 3,000 rupees per month after age 60 years. After death of the subscriber, the scheme pays 50% of the pension to the spouse as family pension. Government adds the same amount as the monthly contribution.
cards.who_can_apply: Small or marginal farmers with cultivable land up to 2 hectares can apply. Applicants are from 18 to 40 years at entry and names appear in land records as on 01.08.2019. Applicants hold Aadhaar card and savings bank account or PM-KISAN account.
cards.documents: Papers needed are Aadhaar card and savings bank account number with IFSC code. Bank passbook or cheque leaf or copy of bank statement works as proof of bank account. The CSC centre will tell you the full list of papers.
cards.how_to_apply: Farmers visit the nearest Common Service Centre for enrolment. Aadhaar card and savings bank account number with IFSC code are taken along with initial contribution in cash. The Village Level Entrepreneur fills details and issues Kisan Card with pension account number.

cards.benefit_text: The scheme gives counselling through helpline and district centres. It gives digital content and training in soft skills and literacy. It gives insurance support and placement support with bridge and language courses.
cards.who_can_apply: The scheme is for people of Indian nationality. People aged between 15 to 45 years with Aadhaar card and Aadhaar linked bank account can apply if job role rules are met.
cards.documents: Papers needed depend on the job role. Aadhaar card is needed for enrolment. An Aadhaar linked bank account is needed. The CSC centre will tell you the full list of papers.
cards.how_to_apply: Interested people contact the nearest Training Center to apply. Aadhaar ID is needed at the time of enrolment. 70% attendance is needed for assessment.

cards.benefit_text: The scheme pays 3,000 rupees after pregnancy registration and one checkup. The scheme pays 2,000 rupees after birth registration and vaccines till 14 weeks. The scheme pays 6,000 rupees for a second child if it is a girl child.
cards.who_can_apply: Pregnant women must be at least 19 years old. The scheme is for the first live birth and for women with wage loss. Women in regular government jobs cannot apply.
cards.documents: Papers needed are Aadhaar card and bank account details. MCP card and child birth certificate are also needed. Child immunization details are needed after birth. The CSC centre will tell you the full list of papers.
cards.how_to_apply: Go to the official website of the Ministry and click Citizen login. Enter mobile number for verification and create an account. Then login and fill beneficiary registration for first child or second child.

cards.benefit_text: The scheme offers loan categories. Shishu covers loans up to Rs.50,000. Kishore covers loans above Rs.50,000 up to Rs.5 lakh. Tarun covers loans above Rs.5 lakh up to Rs.10 lakh. Tarun Plus offers loans up to Rs.20 lakh for entrepreneurs who have repaid Tarun loans.
cards.who_can_apply: Individuals, proprietary concerns, partnership firms, private limited companies, public companies and other legal forms may apply. Applicants must not be defaulters and should have a satisfactory credit track record. Required skills or experience depend on the proposed activity.
cards.documents: Identity proof such as voter ID, PAN or Aadhaar; address proof like recent electricity or telephone bill; recent colour photograph; proof of identity or address of the business enterprise; and, for larger loans, last two years’ balance sheets. The CSC centre will tell you the full list of papers.
cards.how_to_apply: Visit the PM Mudra website and open the Udyamimitra portal. Click “Apply Now”, choose entrepreneur type and register with name, email and mobile to get an OTP. Fill personal and business details, select loan category, attach documents and submit. An application number is generated.

cards.benefit_text: The scheme pays yearly academic allowance. Group 1 pays 13,000 rupees for hostellers and 7,000 rupees for day scholars. Group 2 pays 9,500 rupees and 6,500 rupees. Group 3 pays 6,000 rupees and 3,000 rupees. Group 4 pays 4,000 rupees and 2,500 rupees.
cards.who_can_apply: Indian nationals from Scheduled Castes can apply after passing Matriculation Higher Secondary or higher examination. Parents income from all sources must not exceed 2,50,000 rupees per annum.
cards.documents: Papers include Caste Certificate and Income proof. Papers also include Aadhaar Card and Bank Account Details. The CSC centre will tell you the full list of papers.
cards.how_to_apply: Applicants open the official NSP website and click New Registration under Applicant Corner. Registration starts with Mobile OTP and needs Aadhaar Details and Bank Account Details.

cards.benefit_text: The scheme gives cash assistance of Rs. 1600 for 14.2 kg cylinder and Rs. 1150 for 5 kg cylinder. First LPG refill and stove are free with the deposit free connection.
cards.who_can_apply: Adult women who are 18 years of age can apply. Women belong to SC households, ST households and other poor groups. The household must have no other LPG connection.
cards.documents: The papers are KYC form, Ration Card and Aadhaar. Aadhaar of adult family members is also needed. Bank account number and IFSC is needed. The CSC centre will tell you the full list of papers.
cards.how_to_apply: Forms are available at the nearest LPG distributor. The form is filled with personal details and bank details. The form with papers is submitted at the nearest LPG distributor.

cards.benefit_text: The scheme gives certificate and ID card. Training stipend is ₹ 500 per day. Toolkit grant is ₹ 15,000. Loans are ₹ 1,00,000 and ₹ 2,00,000 at 5% interest. Digital payment incentive is ₹ 1 per transaction up to 100 transactions monthly.
cards.who_can_apply: Artisans and craftspeople working with hands and tools in 18 traditional trades can apply. Applicants must be 18 years or older and work on self-employment basis in unorganized sector. Only one member from a family can apply and government service families cannot apply.
cards.documents: People need Aadhaar card. People need mobile number. People need bank details. People need ration card. The CSC centre will tell you the full list of papers.
cards.how_to_apply: Artisans go to the nearest CSC centre for registration. Workers carry Aadhaar card linked mobile number and bank details. Staff do biometric check and fill the online form.

cards.benefit_text: The scheme provides free or affordable soil tests. The scheme provides timely and accurate soil analysis results. Reports give custom nutrient advice. This helps optimise fertiliser use and lower input costs.
cards.who_can_apply: The scheme is applicable for all farmers in India. It covers all farmers in India.
cards.documents: Documents vary for each state. Farmers consult the relevant authorities for detailed information. The CSC centre will tell you the full list of papers.
cards.how_to_apply: Farmers approach the District Agriculture Officer or Block Agriculture Officer for soil testing. The officer checks if the district or village falls under State Annual Action Plan. An agent collects land details and a soil sample.

cards.benefit_text: The scheme provides subsidies of 50 to 80 percent for purchasing agricultural machinery, helping farmers buy equipment at lower cost and increase yield.
cards.who_can_apply: All landholding farmer families, SHGs, user groups, cooperative societies, FPOs and entrepreneurs who are Indian natives and financially weak can apply. Women farmers receive priority. Applicants must not have taken any other central subsidy.
cards.documents: Aadhar card, passport size photo, Record of Rights of land, first page of bank passbook, and any ID proof such as Aadhar, driving licence, voter ID, PAN or passport. The CSC centre will tell you the full list of papers.
cards.how_to_apply: Visit the portal agrimachinery.nic.in, choose Registration from the dropdown, fill the required information and submit the form online.
